title: Rabbi Aninaya (Inyani, Anyani) bar Sisi (Sisai, Susai)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned only in the Jerusalem Talmud. [Berakhot 7:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.7.2.5): “Rabbi Nasa said: Many times I ate (when I was small) with Rabbi Tachlifa, Father (Hyman considers the word ‘Father’ superfluous, for Rabbi Nasa did not know his father, as in the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Terumot), and with Aninaya bar Sisi, my uncle, and they did not count me [for zimmun] until I had brought two hairs.” (Hyman regards the [Bereshit Rabbah 91:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.91.3) reading as corrupted.)
In [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 6, end of halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.1.11), we find: “Rabbi Inyanu bar Sisai says in the name of Rabbi Liezer.”

In Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, chapter 10, end of halakhah 1: Rabbi Simon is cited as transmitting in the name of Inyani son of Rabbi Sisai; and in [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma, chapter 3, end of halakhah 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.3.5.4): Rabbi Simon transmits in the name of Rabbi Anyani ben Susai.

In [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma, chapter 3, end of halakhah 7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.3.7.8), we find: Rabbi Inyoni bar Susai went up to Rabbi Chanina in Tzippori. Chanina said to him, “Come, and I will transmit it (the Explicit Name) to you.” His son [the father is not specified here] went under the bed; the son sneezed, and Chanina heard his voice. Chanina said, “How do you behave among you — with deceit?” Hyman prefers the reading Anani bar Nachshon in [Kohelet Rabbah 3:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.3.11.3), since Rabbi Aninai belonged to the second and third generations, for Rabbi Simon spoke in his name; if so, how is he connected to Rabbi Chanina of Tzippori — neither the first Rabbi Chanina nor the last Rabbi Chanina, who was much later?

Likewise, what we find in [Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni, chapter 4, end of halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.4.3.8), “Rabbi Inya bar Sasai went up to Rabbi Yona,” Hyman considers a different Amora, for there it is implied that he was younger than Rabbi Yonah. We find Rabbi Shmuel bar Inya: [Eruvin 63b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.63b.7).

notes.text: Berakhot retains Tachlifa abba and has Aninaya as the uncle. The linked Bereshit Rabbah parallel names Rabbi Asi as the speaker and Rabbi Chanina bar Sisi as the uncle. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1484&lang=en) discusses the name variant and sees a connection with Chanina bar Sisi.

In Yoma, Chanina offers to transmit the Name to the visitor. The linked Kohelet Rabbah parallel uses Anani bar Nachshon and its accompanying English takes the hidden boy to be Chanina’s son. Hyman prefers the name in Kohelet Rabbah, and he treats the younger man in the Maaser Sheni episode as someone else. The Inyani citation in Pesachim remains unverified.
